1	On August 28, 2017, Amazon acquired Whole Foods Market, a grocery retailer, for
     2	approximately $13.2 billion.47 After reviewing the proposed acquisition, the FTC determined no
     3	further action was needed at the time.48 Prior to the acquisition, Amazon offered the online
     4	grocery delivery service Amazon Fresh, which launched in 2007,49 and Prime Pantry, which
     5	launched in 2014 and ended in January 2021.50 By acquiring Whole Foods Market, Amazon
     6	obtained brick-and-mortar grocery store locations that it was able to integrate with its online
     7	services.51 For example, shoppers with an Amazon Prime membership52 are eligible for discounts
     8	and free pickup or delivery of Whole Foods Market groceries in selected zip codes,53 and Amazon
     9	Hub Lockers—where consumers can pick up products purchased on Amazon’s website—are
    10	often located in Whole Foods Markets.54
    11	Amazon’s acquisition of Whole Foods Market may have increased competition in the grocery
    12	retail market. Prior to the acquisition, Walmart was the largest grocery retailer, followed by
    13	Kroger.55 Progressive Grocer, a research group, estimates that in 2020, Walmart had the highest
    14	U.S. retail sales of grocery items, followed by Amazon.56 However, Duff & Phelps, a consulting
    15	firm, indicates that Amazon comprises only a small portion of the grocery retail market and that it
    16	serves as “more of a symbolic threat.”57 Nevertheless, other grocery retailers have responded by
    17	implementing changes in response to competitive pressure from Amazon.58
    18	Competitive pressure from Amazon may have incentivized other grocery retailers to start offering
    19	online delivery services. In 2017, the year Amazon acquired Whole Foods, Walmart launched an
    20	online delivery service in selected cities;59 Kroger launched an online delivery service in selected
    21	cities in 2018.60 In 2020, Walmart launched Walmart+,61 a membership delivery service that does
    22	not have a minimum order requirement,62 similar to an Amazon Prime membership. Consumers
    23	may have benefited from food retailers offering their own online delivery services, particularly as
    24	many of these stores offer free delivery on orders over $35. These changes may have also
    25	increased pressure on other online grocery delivery services, such as Instacart, a third-party
    26	service that delivers online groceries from selected stores in selected cities; the service launched
    27	in 2012 and stopped delivering groceries from Whole Foods in 2019.63
    28	Amazon’s acquisition of Whole Foods Market raised concern about its growing dominance in the
    29	retail industry, particularly in e-commerce. According to eMarketer, a market research company,
    30	Amazon had the greatest share of e-commerce sales at 38.7% in 2020; Walmart had the second-
    31	greatest share at 5.3% (Figure 1). The estimate from eMarketer includes all online sales,
    32	including products that Amazon does not offer. The House Subcommittee on Antitrust staff report
    33	finds that by restricting products to those sold on Amazon, a market share of 50% or higher may
    34	be a more credible estimate of Amazon’s share of online sales, and that over 60% of all U.S.
    35	online product searches begin on Amazon.64 Through its acquisition of Whole Foods, Amazon
    36	gained access to additional consumer data, strengthening its bargaining power with suppliers.65 In
    37	addition, Amazon has integrated vertically, such as by offering products under its private label
    38	AmazonBasics and by creating its own delivery system. Amazon has reportedly invested $60
    39	billion since 2014 in its delivery network, including capital leases for warehouses and aircraft; in
    40	2019, it had the fourth-largest share of U.S. package deliveries, behind FedEx, United Parcel
    41	Service, and the U.S. Postal Service.66 By integrating vertically, Amazon may be able to further
    42	strengthen its position in e-commerce; if, for example, it is able to provide faster delivery,67
    43	consumers could benefit even if it becomes more difficult for other companies to compete.
    44	Facebook’s Acquisition of Instagram
    45	Facebook announced that it had reached an agreement to acquire Instagram, a social networking
    46	service (i.e., social media platform), for $1 billion on April 9, 2012.68 The FTC reviewed the
    47	acquisition, and on August 22, 2012, it closed the investigation without taking action.69 On
    48	December 9, 2020, the FTC filed a lawsuit against Facebook, alleging that “Facebook has
    49	maintained its monopoly position by buying up companies that present competitive threats, ” in
    50	addition to imposing restrictive policies against companies it does not acquire.70 A coalition of 46
    51	state attorneys general, led by New York Attorney General Letitia James, filed a parallel lawsuit
    52	against Facebook, also alleging that Facebook acquired companies to eliminate competitive
    53	threats.71 Both lawsuits72 specifically mention Facebook’s acquisitions of Instagram and
    54	WhatsApp, a messaging app for mobile devices.73
    55	Prior to the acquisition, Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg stated in an internal email that
    56	“Instagram has become a large and viable competitor to us on mobile photos, which will
    57	increasingly be the future of photos.”74 This statement has been used to support the claim that
    58	Facebook acquired Instagram with the intention of eliminating a potential competitor.
    59	It is unclear how successful Instagram would have been had it not been acquired by Facebook,
    60	illustrating the difficulty of predicting whether a nascent firm could become a viable competitor.
    61	Instagram was a relatively new company when it was acquired,75 and grew rapidly thereafter,
    62	from about 100 million monthly active users (MAUs) in February 2013 to 500 million MAUs in June 2016
    63	and 1 billion MAUs in June 2018.76 As it grew in popularity, Instagram was able to use
    64	Facebook’s resources, such as its advertising services and its infrastructure, which hosts and
    65	processes large amounts of consumer data. These have been key to the profitability of Instagram,
    66	which hosts a wide range of users, including “influencers”—that is, users with a large number of
    67	followers who are paid by sponsors to market certain products.77 It is possible that without the
    68	merger, Instagram would have been among the platforms that have struggled to compete in digital
    69	markets because of resource constraints. This occurred with the social networking service
    70	Friendster, which turned down a $30 million buyout offer from Google in 2003 but then struggled
    71	with technical difficulties as its user base grew; users left the platform for other social media
    72	sites, and Friendster eventually closed down.78
    73	Another complication in evaluating the effect of Facebook’s acquisition of Instagram is
    74	determining how the market should be defined, particularly in digital markets that can quickly
    75	evolve. Social networking services can include a wide range of platforms. When Facebook
    76	acquired Instagram in 2012, one of the defining features of social networking services—a
    77	category that than included Friendster and Myspace, among others—was the networks users
    78	could create. Users could clearly indicate the users in their respective network(s) on the social
    79	networking service,79 although some may have chosen to keep their network(s) private. At that
    80	time, Instagram was described as a photo-sharing app, arguably competing with apps like
    81	Photobucket and Flickr, rather than with Facebook.

82	Additional types of platforms can be considered social networking services: Reddit allows users
    83	to create communities based on their interests; LinkedIn allows users to create connections for
    84	business and employment opportunities; and TikTok allows users to share short-form videos.80
    85	Some of these platforms allow users to connect with any other user on the platform rather than
    86	only with users in their personal network, focusing on the content rather than the user. These
    87	changes suggest that a user’s ability to create social networks may no longer be the defining
    88	feature of social networking services.
    89	In addition, social networking services are not necessarily substitutes for one another. For
    90	example, although Instagram and Microsoft’s LinkedIn are both typically viewed as social
    91	networking services, it is unlikely that users would substitute one platform for the other. One
    92	report estimates that internet users had an average of about seven social media accounts,
    93	suggesting that some users rely on different social media platforms for different purposes.81

Based on `doc.txt`, the text describes two mergers/acquisitions and their consequences:

**Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods Market (2017, ~$13.2 billion)**
- **Integration of offline and online retail:** Amazon gained brick-and-mortar grocery locations it integrated with its online services — Prime members became eligible for discounts and free pickup/delivery of Whole Foods groceries in selected zip codes, and Amazon Hub Lockers are often located inside Whole Foods stores.
- **Increased competitive pressure in grocery retail:** The acquisition may have increased competition. Other retailers responded: Walmart launched online delivery in 2017, Kroger in 2018, and Walmart+ (a membership delivery service with no minimum order) in 2020. Consumers may have benefited, especially from free delivery on orders over $35. The pressure also affected third-party services like Instacart, which stopped delivering groceries from Whole Foods in 2019.
- **Growing dominance in e-commerce:** The deal raised concern about Amazon's dominance — eMarketer estimated Amazon had 38.7% of e-commerce sales in 2020 (vs. 5.3% for Walmart), and over 60% of U.S. online product searches begin on Amazon.
- **Stronger bargaining power and vertical integration:** Through the acquisition, Amazon gained access to additional consumer data, strengthening its bargaining power with suppliers. Combined with vertical integration (its AmazonBasics private label and its own delivery system, with ~$60 billion invested since 2014 and the fourth-largest U.S. package-delivery share in 2019), Amazon may further strengthen its e-commerce position — potentially benefiting consumers through faster delivery, even if it becomes harder for other companies to compete.

**Facebook's acquisition of Instagram (2012, $1 billion)**
- **Antitrust scrutiny:** The FTC closed its 2012 investigation without action, but in December 2020 the FTC sued Facebook, alleging it maintained its monopoly by buying up companies that posed competitive threats (specifically naming Instagram and WhatsApp); a coalition of 46 state attorneys general filed a parallel suit. Zuckerberg's internal email calling Instagram "a large and viable competitor" was used to support the claim that Facebook acquired it to eliminate a potential competitor.
- **Instagram's rapid growth using Facebook's resources:** Instagram grew from ~100 million monthly active users (Feb 2013) to 500 million (June 2016) and 1 billion (June 2018), leveraging Facebook's advertising services and data infrastructure, which were key to its profitability (including paid "influencer" marketing).
- **Counterfactual uncertainty:** It is unclear how successful Instagram would have been without the merger; it may have struggled from resource constraints, as happened with Friendster, which turned down a $30 million Google buyout in 2003, suffered technical problems as it grew, and eventually closed.
- **Complicated market effects:** Evaluating the merger's effect is complicated by market definition in fast-evolving digital markets — at the time, Instagram was described as a photo-sharing app competing with Photobucket and Flickr rather than Facebook, and social networking services are not necessarily substitutes for one another (one report estimates users hold an average of about seven social media accounts).
